This is especially true in regions like Nigeria, Ghana, and Zimbabwe, where financial isolation restricts access to e-commerce. COREMERCH provides a robust solution with its sovereign commerce infrastructure, enabling you to deploy a fully operational digital store using Cloudflare Pages for free, ensuring automatic crypto payment processing without the need for traditional payment systems.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The COREMERCH infrastructure is designed to empower digital creators by bypassing the limitations imposed by traditional platforms. Platforms like Stripe may lock you out due to regional restrictions, but by utilizing Cloudflare Pages, you gain complete ownership and control over your store. This infrastructure is built to withstand financial crises, currency collapse, and payment rejections, ensuring that you are not dependent on third-party services that can fail you. Instead, you leverage robust, free tools to establish your online presence and conduct transactions securely.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before you can deploy your digital store, you need a few essential components. First, set up a GitHub account to manage your store’s code repository. Next, familiarize yourself with Cloudflare Pages and create an account to host your site. You will also need a NOWPayments account for seamless cryptocurrency payment processing. Finally, gather your digital products—such as ebooks, courses, or designs—ready for upload. By preparing these elements, you position yourself for a smooth deployment process using either Stack 01 or Stack 02.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Once your infrastructure is ready, the next step involves configuring your payment and delivery systems. For Stack 01, integrate NOWPayments with your GitHub Pages site using Google Apps Script for backend logic. This allows you to process cryptocurrency payments securely. Ensure that your product delivery is automated, utilizing storage solutions like Google Drive to host your digital files. For Stack 02, you will utilize Cloudflare Workers alongside Supabase for a more robust backend structure, which can support more products and offer advanced features like SPF/DKIM/DMARC for email deliverability.
Your digital store is yours, built on infrastructure you own.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

After setting up your payment pipeline, it’s time to go live. Deploy your site on Cloudflare Pages and test your payment system using the NOWPayments integration. Make sure to perform transactions on the mainnet to confirm that everything functions as expected. Monitor the entire process closely to capture any issues. Once your first transaction is successful, you’ll have a solid foundation for your digital store, ready to begin serving customers and generating revenue without the limitations of traditional payment systems.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Once your digital store is operational, consider strategies for scaling your offerings. Start by expanding your product line and using the full capabilities of your infrastructure. With Stack 02, you can easily add more products and leverage additional features from Supabase for better data management. Consider marketing strategies to attract traffic to your store, utilizing social media and content marketing. The flexibility of your COREMERCH setup allows you to scale efficiently without the burden of subscription fees or platform dependency.
How do I build a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free?

The setup sequence matters because each component depends on the previous one being correctly configured. Start with NOWPayments: create your account, configure wallet addresses for each coin you want to accept, generate the API key, and note the IPN secret key you will set. Then configure the backend: in Stack 01, deploy the Google Apps Script Web App and note its URL; in Stack 02, deploy the Cloudflare Worker and note its URL. Set that URL as the webhook endpoint in your NOWPayments IPN settings. Then configure the storefront. Then run a real mainnet test — send actual crypto to your configured wallet address, confirm NOWPayments detects it, confirm the webhook fires, and confirm the delivery email arrives with a working download link.
No subscriptions or dependencies; manage your store with confidence.

Both result in the same ownership structure: your GitHub or Cloudflare account, your Supabase database, your NOWPayments account, your wallet, your store. See both options at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Follow the setup sequence without skipping steps — configuration errors are significantly harder to diagnose than setup time. First: create your NOWPayments account, add wallet addresses, generate your API key, and note your IPN secret key. Second: deploy the backend — configure Cloudflare Worker with your NOWPayments credentials and product settings, or configure Google Apps Script with the same — and confirm the endpoint URL. Third: set the webhook endpoint URL in your NOWPayments IPN settings. Fourth: deploy the storefront to Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages and confirm product pages and checkout display correctly. Fifth: configure your custom domain and DNS if using one. Sixth: complete a real mainnet test transaction. Seventh: check the order database for the test entry. Only after steps six and seven pass cleanly should you share the store URL publicly.

Yes, both GitHub Pages and Cloudflare Pages are excellent options for hosting a digital product store. They provide the necessary infrastructure to manage your site without relying on conventional payment systems.

NOWPayments charges a low fee of 0.5% per transaction, making it an economical choice for processing cryptocurrency payments without the complications of traditional payment providers.

To secure your store, utilize HTTPS through Cloudflare Pages, implement proper backend logic with Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, and ensure your payment integration with NOWPayments is correctly configured.
